note: The Checkaverse Gazette, printed fresh on the first visit of each school day from the town's event log. Trainers are named only for good news: catches, evolutions, ghosts brought back, moves learned and battle wins. Deaths and sickness are counted without names. {n} is a count, {trainer} a trainer name, {species} a species, {move} a move. Every line here is written by hand; the overnight director only adds the Around town quotes, and only lines that passed its checks.

quiet.title: A quiet day in the Checkaverse
quiet.body: Nothing much happened yesterday. The tall grass is full, the gym is open and the residents are hard at work. Today is a good day to make some news.

title: The cemetery hill grows by {n}
{n} Checklings laid to rest
one: A Checkling was laid to rest on the cemetery hill
The cemetery hill has a new headstone
deaths.body: The clinic reminds every trainer: check your Care panel every day, and treat sickness early. Too much of anything is as risky as too little.

title: {trainer} brings a ghost back from the hill
A ghost returns with {trainer}
ghost.body: {trainer} caught the ghost of a {species} on the cemetery hill. Ghosts never eat and never get sick, but they fade if they are left out of the party.

title: {n} Checklings caught in the wilds
Busy day in the tall grass: {n} catches
catches.one: A Checkling caught in the wilds

title: {n} new moves learned
The gym was busy
learn.body: {list} learned new moves. Bram says the mini games get easier with practice.
learn.one: A new move learned at the gym

title: {trainer} wins {n} battles
{trainer} tops the battle board
wins.body: The most battle wins yesterday went to {trainer}. The weekly rankings are on the notice board in the plaza.

title: Residents battle {n} times
{resident} wins the residents' rivalry
spars.body: {resident} won {w} of {n} resident battles around town.
